description: Index for generated visual assets. Asset records live in per-module manifests under img/generated/visual-assets/.

style.name: Quantitative finance editorial line
style.base_prompt: Academic editorial illustration for a quantitative financial mathematics course. Use a clean vector-like style with subtle paper texture, precise thin linework, restrained geometric depth, off-white background, deep navy ink, teal data accents, amber highlights, and coral downside-risk accents. Keep the composition clear for a Jupyter Book page, with strong concept readability at small sizes. Avoid photorealism, brand logos, real exchange logos, watermarks, crowded decorative details, and fake interface text.
style.negative_prompt: No stock photo look, no real company logos, no watermarks, no illegible tiny text, no decorative gradients, no over-saturated neon palette, no cartoon characters, no random numbers unless specified, no pseudo-code, no distorted formulas, no misspelled labels.

output_defaults.safe_margin: Keep 7% empty margin on every side; keep all labels inside the central 86% safe area.
output_defaults.line_weight: Use thin but readable 2-4 px lines at final export size.
output_defaults.text_size: Use large labels only; shortest text should stay readable at 760 px display width.
output_defaults.postprocess: If the generator cannot create the exact size, generate the nearest larger canvas, then crop or pad to the exact recommended_size before saving.
output_defaults.book_display: The book may display figures narrower than the source file, but the saved source image must keep the recommended_size.

quality_gate: The concept must be understandable without relying on the old image.
Any mathematical label must be exact; reject and regenerate if text is misspelled or formulas are distorted.
Use short labels only; put long explanations in the notebook text or caption, not inside the image.
Avoid real brands, exchange logos, screenshots, and copyrighted visual references.
Keep a consistent white/off-white margin so figures do not look cramped inside the book.
